sections.title: Starting Brawler
paragraphs: Shelly is the starting Brawler and a Damage Dealer. Her defining mechanic is a spread of shotgun pellets: landing several pellets on one target matters more than reading one projectile’s damage as the whole attack. Character art and skin rarity do not by themselves describe combat strength.

sections.title: Buckshot and Super Shell
paragraphs: Buckshot fires a spreading pellet attack. Super Shell adds knockback and destroys cover. The community reference notes that pellets disappear after breaking a wall tile, so removing cover does not mean every pellet then reaches a target behind it. Count the obstruction when planning a follow-up.

sections.title: Spacing practice
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: practise the same shot at near, middle and outer range in the training area, observing how many pellets connect. Then practise holding Super until a threat commits. A useful replay question is whether the Super created a safe follow-up or merely pushed the target out of your effective reach.

sections.title: Progression and loadout
paragraphs: Shelly is available at the beginning of play. Open her Brawler page to inspect the equipped Gadget, Star Power and Hypercharge rather than assuming an old video has your exact kit. Supercell’s Hypercharge support page explains where to inspect the enhanced Super effect after it is unlocked.

sections.title: Cooldowns require a version
paragraphs: Supercell’s June 2026 notes changed Fast Forward’s cooldown and Shell Shock’s slow. A community page can retain older numbers after a patch. This dossier therefore explains the mechanics and records the historical change separately; it does not label any damage, cooldown or win rate as a freshly playtested live value.

history.label: June 2026 · documented tuning
history.detail: The release notes reduce Fast Forward’s cooldown from 20 to 16 seconds and describe Shell Shock as a percentage-based slow. These are that update’s changes, not proof that no later adjustment occurred.

sections.title: Colt’s role
paragraphs: Colt is a Rare Damage Dealer whose Six-Shooters attack sends six shots along a straight line. The important distinction is a sequence of hits rather than one wide splash. His Bullet Storm Super extends the line of fire and can remove cover, changing the space available to both teams.

sections.title: Gadget and Star Power choices
paragraphs: Supercell’s rework description gives Speedloader two slowing shots; it is not the older instant reload described in legacy guides. Silver Bullet pierces Brawlers and removes terrain while consuming ammo. Slick Boots affects movement, while Magnum Special affects range and projectile speed. Buffies add separate effects and should be labelled separately.

sections.title: Track a moving target
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: practise aiming along an opponent’s movement rather than repeatedly firing at their previous position. Review one burst at a time: which shots missed, and did your own movement pull the line away? Before destroying a wall, decide whether opening that lane helps your team or gives enemies an easier approach.

sections.title: Unlocking in the documented system
paragraphs: The August 2026 official notes move Rare and Super Rare unlocks into Brawler Blast, replacing the older Trophy Road route. Check the Brawler Collection’s current unlock screen for your account. This is progression guidance, not a promise that a specific random opening will give Colt.

sections.title: Do not treat missing values as zero
paragraphs: The provider’s ability text can omit numeric values. Missing damage or speed figures are unknown, not zero. Use the game client for the equipped level and Buffie state, and do not compare a community percentage lacking context with a different patch or an unmodified Brawler.

sections.title: Support identity
paragraphs: Poco is a Rare Support Brawler. His guitar-themed Power Chord sends a broad sound-wave attack, and Encore is a healing Super. The useful question is which teammates can benefit from his position, not simply whether he can win a damage race against a solo opponent.

sections.title: Healing and utility
paragraphs: The August 2026 official rework makes Power Chord heal allies by default; Da Capo adds healing rather than enabling it from nothing. Tuning Fork provides healing pulses, while Protective Tunes creates an area against adverse effects. Screeching Solo adds enemy damage to Encore, and Buffies introduce further conditional benefits.

sections.title: Position for two jobs
paragraphs: GameBreak suggestion: practise an angle that lets you pressure an enemy while keeping a teammate in your support area. Watch allied health before spending Super, and identify an exit if the frontline collapses. Review whether a heal prevented a defeat or merely restored safe damage that would already recover later.

sections.title: Progression and equipped kit
paragraphs: Check Brawler Blast in the Brawler Collection for the documented Rare unlock path. After unlocking Poco, verify which Gadget, Star Power and Buffies are actually equipped. A video showing a protected area or extra Super damage may be demonstrating upgrades your own account does not yet have.

sections.title: Old guides describe a different kit
paragraphs: Older explanations that require Da Capo for every normal-attack heal no longer match the cited rework. Numerical healing in a provider response can also be incomplete. Keep the source date and equipped level visible, and treat the history below as a documented revision rather than a complete current balance table.

history.detail: Supercell records baseline allied healing for Power Chord, revised Tuning Fork and Protective Tunes, and Poco’s Buffies. This records the published redesign; later tuning still needs separate review.
